title: Loops
bridge: C++ has `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)`, `while (cond)`, and the range-for `for (char c : text)` that walks through every item. `break` leaves a loop, `continue` skips to the next round. Same shapes as Java, C# and JavaScript.

exercises.title: Count vowels
exercises.prompt: Write int countVowels(std::string s): how many a, e, i, o, u it has (upper or lower case).
hints: char l = std::tolower(c); if (l == 'a' || l == 'e' || ...) count++;

exercises.title: Countdown
exercises.prompt: Read a number n, print n down to 1 (one per line), then Go!

quiz.q: How many times does for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) run?

quiz.why: It skips the rest of this round.

quiz.q: Which loop walks every char in a string?

explain: Explain loops to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
